about.description: Devanilayam is a free, ad-free devotional library of Hindu slokas, ashtotaras and stotras in English, Telugu and Hindi.

mission.title: Our mission
mission.body: Devanilayam exists to make devotional texts easy to read, understand and practice — without advertising, tracking or paywalls standing between you and the verse. The sacred texts themselves are in the public domain, and they should be freely available to everyone who wants to read them.

whatsHere.title: What you will find here
whatsHere.slokas: Slokas and stotras, presented with the verse and its meaning side by side.
whatsHere.ashtotaras: Ashtottara Shatanamavali — the 108 sacred names of each deity, in an uninterrupted flow.
whatsHere.blogs: Readings and reflections on the stories behind the verses.

languages.title: Languages and scripts
languages.body: Every section is available in English, Telugu and Hindi. Devotional text is presented in the script it is chanted in, not merely transliterated, because the reading matters as much as the meaning.

free.title: Free and ad-free
free.body: There are no advertisements, no accounts and no trackers selling your reading habits. The site works offline once opened, and can be installed to your home screen like an app.

contribute.title: Contribute
contribute.body: Devanilayam is open source. Corrections to a verse, a translation or a transliteration are the most valuable contributions of all — if you spot an error, please report it.

contact.title: Contact
contact.body: Questions, corrections and suggestions are welcome. The fastest way to reach the maintainers is to open an issue on the project.

maintainers.title: Who maintains this
maintainers.body: Devanilayam is built and maintained by Mouli Bheemaneti, with contributions from the community.

festivals.subtitle: Every major Hindu festival of the year on one calendar. Tap any day to read what it means and how it is kept.

seo.title: Hindu Festival Calendar 2026 & 2027
seo.description: A simple Hindu festival calendar for 2026 and 2027 with the meaning of each day in English, Telugu and Hindi. Sankranti, Ugadi, Deepavali, Onam, Navratri and more.

festivals.noFestivals: No festivals fall in this month.

makar-sankranti.name: Makar Sankranti · Pongal · Sankranti
makar-sankranti.significance: The sun turns north into Capricorn, ending the long nights and beginning the half of the year the tradition calls Uttarayana. It is a thanksgiving for the harvest that has just come in.
makar-sankranti.observance: The first rice of the season is boiled with jaggery until it spills over, sesame and jaggery sweets are shared, and kites go up across the north.

maha-shivaratri.name: Maha Shivaratri
maha-shivaratri.significance: The great night of Shiva, kept as the night he appeared as the endless pillar of light and as the night he drank the world's poison to save it.
maha-shivaratri.observance: Devotees fast through the day and stay awake through the night, bathing the Shiva linga in milk, water and bilva leaves in four watches until dawn.

holi.name: Holi
holi.significance: The festival of colour and of spring, marking the burning away of the old year's ill will and the play of Krishna with the cowherds of Vrindavan.
holi.observance: Coloured powder and water are thrown freely in the streets, old quarrels are declared over, and gujiya and thandai are shared.

sri-rama-navami.name: Sri Rama Navami
sri-rama-navami.significance: The birth of Rama at Ayodhya, at noon on the ninth day of Chaitra. He is remembered as the one who kept his word at every cost.
sri-rama-navami.observance: The Ramayana is read, the wedding of Rama and Sita is enacted in temples, and panakam and vada pappu are offered and shared.

akshaya-tritiya.name: Akshaya Tritiya
akshaya-tritiya.significance: A day said to be imperishable — whatever is begun or given on it is believed never to diminish. It needs no auspicious hour of its own.
akshaya-tritiya.observance: New ventures are started, gold and grain are bought, and food and water are given away in the belief that such giving never runs out.

buddha-purnima.name: Buddha Purnima
buddha-purnima.significance: The full moon on which the Buddha was born, reached awakening and passed away — three turning points on one day.
buddha-purnima.observance: Temples are lit and decorated, the sutras are recited, and the day is kept with vegetarian food, charity and acts of kindness to animals.

guru-purnima.name: Guru Purnima
guru-purnima.significance: The full moon set aside for the teacher, honouring Veda Vyasa, who arranged the Vedas and gave the tradition its shape.
guru-purnima.observance: Students visit their teachers, offer flowers and a token gift, and take up the year's study or practice afresh.

raksha-bandhan.name: Raksha Bandhan
raksha-bandhan.significance: A thread tied on the wrist stands for protection asked for and promised — most often between a sister and a brother, but given to anyone taken into that trust.
raksha-bandhan.observance: The rakhi is tied after aarti and a sweet, and the one who receives it gives a gift and a promise to stand by the giver.

krishna-janmashtami.name: Krishna Janmashtami
krishna-janmashtami.significance: The midnight birth of Krishna in the prison at Mathura, and the beginning of the life that gave the world the Bhagavad Gita.
krishna-janmashtami.observance: The fast is kept until midnight, when the infant is bathed and cradled; butter and curd are offered, and pots of curd are broken in the streets.

ganesh-chaturthi.name: Ganesh Chaturthi · Vinayaka Chavithi
ganesh-chaturthi.significance: The birthday of Ganesha, who is asked first at every beginning because he is the one who clears what stands in the way.
ganesh-chaturthi.observance: A clay image is brought home and worshipped for a day to eleven, with modak, twenty-one blades of durva grass, and immersion at the end.

sharad-navratri.name: Sharad Navratri
sharad-navratri.significance: Nine nights given to the Goddess in her three aspects — Durga for strength, Lakshmi for plenty, Saraswati for learning.
sharad-navratri.observance: A pot is installed on the first morning and lit for nine days; there is fasting, garba and dandiya in the west, and Bommala Koluvu in the south.

vijayadashami.name: Vijayadashami · Dasara
vijayadashami.significance: The tenth day, when Rama defeated Ravana and Durga defeated Mahishasura — in both stories, the day a long fight was finally won.
vijayadashami.observance: Effigies of Ravana are burnt in the north; in the south children are started on their letters, and tools and instruments are blessed.

dhanteras.name: Dhanteras
dhanteras.significance: The day Dhanvantari rose from the churning of the ocean bearing the pot of amrita, and the opening of the Deepavali days.
dhanteras.observance: Something metal is bought for the house, the first lamp of the season is lit at the door, and the threshold is drawn with rangoli.

naraka-chaturdashi.name: Naraka Chaturdashi · Choti Diwali
naraka-chaturdashi.significance: Krishna's defeat of Narakasura at dawn. In much of the south this, and not the following night, is Deepavali itself.
naraka-chaturdashi.observance: The family rises before sunrise for an oil bath, new clothes are worn, and the first crackers of the festival are lit at first light.

deepavali.name: Deepavali · Diwali
deepavali.significance: The festival of lights, kept for Rama's return to Ayodhya after fourteen years and for Lakshmi, who is said to enter a house that is clean and lit.
deepavali.observance: The house is cleaned and every doorway lamp lit, Lakshmi puja is done in the evening, and sweets are carried to neighbours.

bhai-dooj.name: Bhai Dooj · Bhai Phota
bhai-dooj.significance: Yama visited his sister Yamuna on this day and she marked his forehead; the day closes the Deepavali week on that note of family.
bhai-dooj.observance: A sister applies tilak to her brother's forehead, prays for his long life, and feeds him a meal she has made herself.

bhogi.name: Bhogi
bhogi.significance: The first day of the Sankranti days, when what is worn out is given to the fire so the new year begins with nothing old carried into it.
bhogi.observance: A bonfire is lit before dawn with things no longer needed, and children have Bhogi Pallu — berries and coins — poured over their heads.

kanuma.name: Kanuma
kanuma.significance: The third of the Sankranti days, kept for the cattle that pull the plough and carry the harvest — the year's thanks paid to the animals.
kanuma.observance: Cattle are washed, their horns painted and garlanded, and led in procession; in villages there are bull races and cock fights.

ratha-saptami.name: Ratha Saptami
ratha-saptami.significance: The sun's chariot turns north on this seventh day, treated as Surya's own birthday and the true start of the warm season.
ratha-saptami.observance: A bath is taken at sunrise with arka leaves on the head and shoulders, and rice cooked in milk is offered to the rising sun.

thaipusam.name: Thaipusam
thaipusam.significance: The day Parvati gave Murugan the vel, the spear with which he defeated Surapadman — kept as the victory of clear resolve over pride.
thaipusam.observance: Devotees fast, shave their heads and carry the kavadi in procession to Murugan's hill temples, often on foot through the night.

ugadi.name: Ugadi
ugadi.significance: The Telugu and Kannada new year, the first day of Chaitra. The year's panchangam is read out, setting what lies ahead.
ugadi.observance: Ugadi pachadi is made with six tastes together — sweet, sour, salt, bitter, pungent, tart — because the year will hold all six.

tamil-puthandu.name: Tamil Puthandu
tamil-puthandu.significance: The Tamil new year, on the sun's entry into Aries. It opens the month of Chithirai and the solar year.
tamil-puthandu.observance: The kanni is arranged the night before so it is the first thing seen on waking, and mangai pachadi of six tastes is served.

vishu.name: Vishu
vishu.significance: The Malayali new year and the day of equal light. What the eyes fall on first is believed to set the tone of the year.
vishu.observance: The Vishukkani — rice, gold, a mirror, konna flowers, a lamp before Krishna — is arranged at night and looked at first thing at dawn.

narasimha-jayanti.name: Narasimha Jayanti
narasimha-jayanti.significance: Vishnu came as Narasimha at dusk on this day, neither man nor beast, to keep a boon intact and still protect the child Prahlada.
narasimha-jayanti.observance: The fast is kept through the day and broken at sunset, the hour of the appearance, with the Narasimha stotras recited.

varalakshmi-vratam.name: Varalakshmi Vratam
varalakshmi-vratam.significance: The Friday before the Shravana full moon, kept for Lakshmi in her boon-giving form, for the health and wellbeing of the household.
varalakshmi-vratam.observance: A kalasham is decorated as the Goddess, the sacred thread is tied on the wrist, and married women invite each other for tamboolam.

onam.name: Onam · Thiruvonam
onam.significance: Kerala's harvest festival and the day the good king Mahabali is allowed back to see that his people are still well.
onam.observance: Pookalam flower carpets are laid for ten days, the Onasadya is served on a banana leaf, and there are vallam kali boat races.

bathukamma.name: Saddula Bathukamma
bathukamma.significance: The last and largest night of Telangana's flower festival, honouring Gauri in the seasonal blooms of the countryside.
bathukamma.observance: Flowers are stacked into a conical bathukamma, women circle it singing through the evening, and it is set afloat on water at night.

ayudha-puja.name: Ayudha Puja · Saraswati Puja
ayudha-puja.significance: The ninth day of Navratri, when the tools of a trade are honoured as the means by which the household is kept.
ayudha-puja.observance: Books, instruments, machines and vehicles are cleaned, decorated with turmeric and flowers, and left unused for the day.

karthika-deepam.name: Karthika Deepam · Kartika Purnima
karthika-deepam.significance: The full moon of Karthika, when Shiva stood as the pillar of fire whose top and bottom could not be found.
karthika-deepam.observance: Lamps are lit in every doorway and floated on tanks and rivers; the great beacon is lit on the hill at Tiruvannamalai.

vaikunta-ekadashi.name: Vaikunta Ekadashi · Mukkoti Ekadashi
vaikunta-ekadashi.significance: The one day the northern gate of Vaikuntha is said to stand open. Passing through it is held to be the release of a lifetime.
vaikunta-ekadashi.observance: A full fast and a night awake; before dawn devotees queue to pass through the Vaikuntha Dwaram at Tirumala, Srirangam and elsewhere.

lohri.name: Lohri
lohri.significance: Punjab's midwinter fire, marking the end of the coldest days and the sugarcane harvest that comes in with them.
lohri.observance: A bonfire is lit at dusk and circled while sesame, jaggery, popcorn and rewri are thrown into it; the year's newborns are welcomed by name.

vasant-panchami.name: Vasant Panchami
vasant-panchami.significance: The first day of spring, given to Saraswati, from whom learning, speech and music are asked.
vasant-panchami.observance: Yellow is worn, books and instruments are placed before the Goddess, and small children are helped to write their first letters.

holika-dahan.name: Holika Dahan
holika-dahan.significance: The night before Holi, when Holika burned and the child Prahlada walked out of the fire unhurt — trust outlasting the harm meant for it.
holika-dahan.observance: A pyre is built at the crossroads and lit after moonrise; families circle it, and new grain is roasted in the embers.

chaitra-navratri.name: Chaitra Navratri
chaitra-navratri.significance: Nine nights of the Goddess opening the lunar new year, ending on the day Rama was born.
chaitra-navratri.observance: The pot is installed and barley sown on the first day; the fast is kept for nine days and broken with the kanya puja on the eighth or ninth.

hanuman-jayanti.name: Hanuman Jayanti
hanuman-jayanti.significance: The birth of Hanuman, whose strength was never his own point — it was always placed at the service of Rama.
hanuman-jayanti.observance: The Hanuman Chalisa is read forty times or more, sindoor and oil are offered, and boondi and bananas are distributed.

baisakhi.name: Baisakhi · Vaisakhi
baisakhi.significance: Punjab's harvest day, and the day in 1699 that Guru Gobind Singh founded the Khalsa at Anandpur Sahib.
baisakhi.observance: The Guru Granth Sahib is read through, nagar kirtan processions go out, and bhangra and gidda are danced on the cut fields.

shani-jayanti.name: Shani Jayanti
shani-jayanti.significance: The appearance of Shani, the son of Surya, who is the slow and exact keeper of the account of one's own actions.
shani-jayanti.observance: Sesame oil is offered at his shrine, black sesame and iron are given in charity, and the Shani stotram is recited on the Saturday.

vat-savitri.name: Vat Savitri Vrat
vat-savitri.significance: Savitri argued Yama into returning her husband's life on this day; the banyan she waited under stands for a life that keeps going.
vat-savitri.observance: Married women fast, circle a banyan tree winding thread around it, and hear the story of Savitri and Satyavan.

nag-panchami.name: Nag Panchami
nag-panchami.significance: The serpents are honoured on this day — as guardians of the fields and the water, and as the ornament Shiva wears without fear.
nag-panchami.observance: Milk and puffed rice are offered at anthills and serpent stones, and no digging or ploughing of the earth is done.

hartalika-teej.name: Hartalika Teej
hartalika-teej.significance: Parvati's fast to win Shiva, kept the day before Ganesh Chaturthi. It stands for a choice held to when everything argued against it.
hartalika-teej.observance: Women fast without food or water through the day and night, make sand images of Shiva and Parvati, and stay awake singing until dawn.

karva-chauth.name: Karva Chauth
karva-chauth.significance: A fast kept from sunrise to moonrise for the long life of a husband, on the fourth day after the Sharad full moon.
karva-chauth.observance: The sargi is eaten before dawn; at night the moon is seen through a sieve, then the husband's face, and he gives the first sip of water.

govardhan-puja.name: Govardhan Puja · Annakut
govardhan-puja.significance: Krishna lifted the Govardhan hill on his finger for seven days to shelter Vraj from the rain — the day the ordinary hill was honoured over the storm.
govardhan-puja.observance: A hill of food is built before the deity and offered as annakut, and cattle are washed, garlanded and fed first.

chhath-puja.name: Chhath Puja
chhath-puja.significance: Four days of thanks to the setting and rising sun and to Chhathi Maiya, kept without a priest and without an image.
chhath-puja.observance: A fast without water is held for over thirty hours; the family stands in the river at sunset and again at sunrise to offer arghya.

gudi-padwa.name: Gudi Padwa
gudi-padwa.significance: The Marathi new year and the first day of Chaitra, remembered as the day Rama returned to Ayodhya and the day the world was made.
gudi-padwa.observance: A gudi — a bright cloth, neem leaves and a garland over an upturned pot on a pole — is raised at the window, and shrikhand puri is eaten.

poila-boishakh.name: Poila Boishakh
poila-boishakh.significance: The Bengali new year, opening the month of Boishakh and, traditionally, the year's accounts.
poila-boishakh.observance: Traders open the new ledger with the haal khata, homes are drawn with alpona, and the day is spent in new clothes and visiting.

bohag-bihu.name: Bohag Bihu · Rongali Bihu
bohag-bihu.significance: Assam's spring new year and the start of the sowing, the most joyful of the three Bihus.
bohag-bihu.observance: Cattle are bathed in turmeric on the first day and people greet each other on the second; the Bihu dance and husori songs go on for days.

jagannath-rath-yatra.name: Jagannath Rath Yatra
jagannath-rath-yatra.significance: Jagannath, Balabhadra and Subhadra leave the temple at Puri for their aunt's shrine — the one time the deities come out to the street.
jagannath-rath-yatra.observance: Three tall wooden chariots are built afresh each year and pulled along the Grand Road by the crowd itself, over some three kilometres.

anant-chaturdashi.name: Anant Chaturdashi · Ganesh Visarjan
anant-chaturdashi.significance: The fourteenth day, kept for Vishnu as Ananta, the endless. It is also the day the Ganesh festival closes.
anant-chaturdashi.observance: A fourteen-knotted thread is tied on the wrist, and the Ganesh images are carried in procession and immersed in water.

mahalaya-amavasya.name: Mahalaya Amavasya
mahalaya-amavasya.significance: The last day of the fortnight of the ancestors and the eve of Durga Puja — the day the Goddess is invited to begin her journey home.
mahalaya-amavasya.observance: Tarpan is offered to the ancestors at the river before dawn, and the Mahishasura Mardini recital is heard at daybreak.

durga-puja.name: Durga Puja
durga-puja.significance: Bengal's great autumn festival, keeping the days Durga spends at her parents' home before returning to Kailash.
durga-puja.observance: Pandals open from Shashthi, dhak drums play through the days, and the image is taken for immersion on Vijaya Dashami.
